svg.title: Four Checks Before Assigning a Crew
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-preflight-labor-chemical-and-contract-checks; chart type: decision_tree; title: Four Checks Before Assigning a Crew; subtitle: Each failed check routes to a specific correction before the affected work starts.; chapter number: 5; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Read nodes in order. Each numeric value is a sequence index, not a risk score or probability. Apply federal requirements alongside applicable state and local rules. Insurance limits depend on jurisdiction, policy terms, and the buyer's contract.; caption: A signed cleaning agreement does not cure underpaid labor, misclassification, unsafe chemical use, or uninsured scope.; stages: label: Wages and paid time; value: Pass to classification; otherwise recost and correct payroll; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Apply 29 U.S.C. 206 and 207 to covered workers, including overtime for covered nonexempt employees. Keep required records under 29 CFR Part 516 and evaluate compensable time under 29 CFR Part 785. Capture intersite travel and setup; apply higher applicable state or local wage requirements.; label: Actual worker relationship; value: Pass to chemical review; otherwise redesign or employ; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Evaluate actual control and economic facts under applicable FLSA, tax, and state tests, including 26 U.S.C. 3121(d)(2) and California Labor Code section 2775 where relevant. A 1099 form, LLC, or insurance certificate alone does not establish independent status.; label: Chemical and exposure controls; value: Pass to contract review; otherwise train and correct methods; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Implement applicable 29 CFR 1910.1200 labeling, safety data sheets, written program, and training requirements. Follow disinfectant labeling under 7 U.S.C. 136j. Where occupational exposure exists, implement 29 CFR 1910.1030 controls; do not assign untrained workers to sharps or blood cleanup.; label: Insured and bounded scope; value: Start covered work only after resolving identified coverage gaps; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Confirm required workers' compensation and buyer-specified liability coverage with the broker. Review exclusions, endorsements, key loss, property damage, and medical-site activities. Attach service frequencies, inspection standards, change-order pricing, payment terms, and termination rights to the signed agreement.

text.title: Four Checks Before Assigning a Crew
text.tspan: Four Checks Before Assigning a Crew

circle.title: label: Wages and paid time; value: Pass to classification; otherwise recost and correct payroll; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Apply 29 U.S.C. 206 and 207 to covered workers, including overtime for covered nonexempt employees. Keep required records under 29 CFR Part 516 and evaluate compensable time under 29 CFR Part 785. Capture intersite travel and setup; apply higher applicable state or local wage requirements.

text.title: Apply 29 U.S.C. 206 and 207 to covered workers, including overtime for covered nonexempt employees. Keep required records under 29 CFR Part 516 and evaluate compensable time under 29 CFR Part 785. Capture intersite travel and setup; apply higher applicable state or local wage requirements.

circle.title: label: Actual worker relationship; value: Pass to chemical review; otherwise redesign or employ; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Evaluate actual control and economic facts under applicable FLSA, tax, and state tests, including 26 U.S.C. 3121(d)(2) and California Labor Code section 2775 where relevant. A 1099 form, LLC, or insurance certificate alone does not establish independent status.

text.title: Evaluate actual control and economic facts under applicable FLSA, tax, and state tests, including 26 U.S.C. 3121(d)(2) and California Labor Code section 2775 where relevant. A 1099 form, LLC, or insurance certificate alone does not establish independent status.

circle.title: label: Chemical and exposure controls; value: Pass to contract review; otherwise train and correct methods; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Implement applicable 29 CFR 1910.1200 labeling, safety data sheets, written program, and training requirements. Follow disinfectant labeling under 7 U.S.C. 136j. Where occupational exposure exists, implement 29 CFR 1910.1030 controls; do not assign untrained workers to sharps or blood cleanup.

text.title: Implement applicable 29 CFR 1910.1200 labeling, safety data sheets, written program, and training requirements. Follow disinfectant labeling under 7 U.S.C. 136j. Where occupational exposure exists, implement 29 CFR 1910.1030 controls; do not assign untrained workers to sharps or blood cleanup.

circle.title: label: Insured and bounded scope; value: Start covered work only after resolving identified coverage gaps; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Confirm required workers' compensation and buyer-specified liability coverage with the broker. Review exclusions, endorsements, key loss, property damage, and medical-site activities. Attach service frequencies, inspection standards, change-order pricing, payment terms, and termination rights to the signed agreement.

text.title: Confirm required workers' compensation and buyer-specified liability coverage with the broker. Review exclusions, endorsements, key loss, property damage, and medical-site activities. Attach service frequencies, inspection standards, change-order pricing, payment terms, and termination rights to the signed agreement.

Assumptions: Read nodes in order. Each numeric value is a sequence index, not a risk score or probability. Apply federal requirements alongside applicable state and local rules. Insurance limits depend on jurisdiction, policy terms, and the buyer's contract.
